text:
- [IARC.1.12] **Consistent `ds_result_t` at every call site.**
  Every libds function that can fail — public API, internal
  module-to-module, static helpers — returns
  `ds_result_t`. No status as an `int`, no thread-local
  errno, no "success-return / call-again-for-detail"
  two-step. A function that cannot fail returns its value or
  nothing: `ds_free`, `ds_build_capabilities`, and the visitor callbacks libds calls
  for each node, edge, trace step or refraction entry
  (`libds.h` declares each `void`), are such functions. One pattern to learn; one pattern to
  review; nothing to translate at the public /
  internal boundary.

  Its shape is a status and a detail and nothing else
  ([IERR.1.3]): 16 bytes, which fits in registers under SysV x86-64
  (RAX:RDX) and AAPCS64. No status carries a source
  location: libds parses no DS source, and an author's
  source location comes from the artefact's `LineSpan`
  atoms ([NDBG.3.1]). The status enum is [IERR.2],
  detail-string stability [IERR.4]. Wire-error propagation is not part of it —
  libds defines no wire encoding for error codes
  ([IERR.6.1]).

  The corollary that the engine's pending-error
  slot preserves first-error-wins for sibling RHS
  actions (where the later sibling succeeds — the
  trampoline only overwrites pending on non-OK,
  and `wm.c`'s save-and-restore around
  `ds_engine_assert` keeps the prior error
  intact across nested calls per IDSP.1.6) is
  pinned in `spec/test_arch_invariants_spec`.

  This decision fixes only the shape and the
  one-everywhere discipline: a failure is never reported
  any other way.
